bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version

import pty, os, sys, subprocess, time, select

def run_with_pty(cmd, input_bytes=b"", timeout=2):
    # returns output
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        # child
        os.execvp(cmd[0], cmd)
    else:
        # parent
        output = b""
        start = time.time()
        while time.time() - start < timeout:
            r, w, e = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.1)
            if r:
                try:
                    data = os.read(fd, 1024)
                    if not data:
                        break
                    output += data
                except OSError:
                    break
        # try to kill child
        try:
            os.kill(pid, 9)
        except:
            pass
        os.close(fd)
        try:
            os.waitpid(pid, 0)
        except:
            pass
        return output

#!/bin/sh

done

chmod +x /tmp/fakebin/ping6

#   - Also need to check resolution for IP literals: if -4 and host is IPv6 literal, fail immediate.

#   - Then spawn `ping -O -i<interval> [-I interface] [ping-args] <host>`

Clap parses float, but ping arg formatting: we need to see if gping formats as `format!("{}", interval)` or with specific?
#   - Example: -n 0.123 => -i0.1 ? Earlier we tested -n 0.123 gave -i0.1 (it rounded/truncated?). Let's retest more.
rm -rf /tmp/fakebin; mkdir -p /tmp/fakebin
cat > /tmp/fakebin/ping <<'EOS'
#!/bin/sh
if [ "$1" = "-V" ]; then echo "ping utility, iputils-s20210722"; exit 0; fi
echo "[ping] $@" >> /tmp/fake_ping.log
while true; do sleep 0.5; echo "64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=1 ttl=64 time=10 ms"; done
EOS
chmod +x /tmp/fakebin/ping
ln -sf ping /tmp/fakebin/ping6

for iv in "0.2" "0.5" "0.123" "0.124" "0.125" "0.126" "1" "1.0" "0.05" "0.001"; do
  rm -f /tmp/fake_ping.log
  PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 ./executable -n $iv 127.0.0.1 2>&1 || true
  cat /tmp/fake_ping.log || echo "no log"
  echo "input $iv"
done

PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 ./executable -i eth0 --ping-args="-Q 2 -c 1" 127.0.0.1 2>&1 || true
cat /tmp/fake_ping.log; rm -f /tmp/fake_ping.log

PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 ./executable --ping-args="-Q 2 -c 1" -i eth0 127.0.0.1 2>&1 || true

PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 ./executable --ping-args="-Q 2" --ping-args="-c 1" 127.0.0.1 2>&1 || true
cat /tmp/fake_ping.log; rm -f /tmp/fake_ping.log

PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 ./executable 127.0.0.1 --ping-args="-Q 2" 2>&1 || true
cat /tmp/fake_ping.log; rm -f /tmp/fake_ping.log

# We saw earlier simple. Need to understand better: does it run shell -c "command"? Probably uses `sh -c <cmd>`.
# Let's test cmd that prints output, check if output captured?
PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH /workspace/executable --help 2>&1 | head

# - TUI with ratatui or tui-rs
# - Graph with braille characters by default, dots when -s
# - Shows header per host with stats: last, min, max, avg, jtr, p95, t/o
# - Uses 30 seconds buffer by default, -b controls seconds.
# - Watch interval -n controls how often to ping? Actually ping interval is controlled via -i to ping binary, but also gping's own refresh interval? For cmd mode, watch-interval is how often to run command.
# - Need to understand cmd mode timing: it runs command via shell and measures execution time.
# - Graph: vertical axis ms, horizontal axis time.
# - Need to replicate clear flag: clears screen after exit via crossterm?

# Let's examine more TUI details via tmux captures
cat > /tmp/fakebin/ping <<'EOS'

if [ "$1" = "-V" ]; then echo "ping utility, iputils-s20210722"; exit 0; fi
h=""
for a in "$@"; do h="$a"; done

EOS

sleep 2
tmux capture-pane -p -t gping_test
tmux kill-server

# Test horizontal margin effect

sleep 2
tmux capture-pane -p -t gping_test | cat -A | head -n 40
tmux kill-server
"}

PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 $BIN 127.0.0.1 --ping-args -c 5 2>&1; echo "exit:$?"; cat /tmp/fake_ping.log 2>&1; rm -f /tmp/fake_ping.log

PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 $BIN 127.0.0.1 --ping-args="-c 5" 2>&1; echo "exit:$?"; cat /tmp/fake_ping.log 2>&1; rm -f /tmp/fake_ping.log

echo "=== Test -4 with IPv4 ok ==="
rm -f /tmp/fake_ping.log
PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 $BIN -4 127.0.0.1 2>&1; echo "exit:$?"; cat /tmp/fake_ping.log 2>&1; rm -f /tmp/fake_ping.log

echo "=== Test -6 with IPv4 fail ==="

echo "=== Test -4 with IPv6 fail ==="

echo "=== Test cloud aws ==="

PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 $BIN aws:eu-west-1 2>&1; echo "exit:$?"; cat /tmp/fake_ping.log 2>&1; rm -f /tmp/fake_ping.log

echo "=== Test cloud gcp ==="
rm -f /tmp/fake_ping.log
PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 $BIN gcp:us-central1 2>&1; echo "exit:$?"; cat /tmp/fake_ping.log 2>&1; rm -f /tmp/fake_ping.log

echo "=== Test invalid host ==="
PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 $BIN invalidhost 2>&1; echo "exit:$?"

echo "dummy"

PATH=/tmp/fakebin:$PATH timeout 0.6 $BIN 127.0.0.1 2>&1; echo "exit:$?"

#!/bin/sh
